# Wahaj Ahmed

Full-stack engineer based in Islamabad, Pakistan. I build React and Node
systems that hold up past 100,000 users. Contact: wahmed@outsentia.com

## Current role

Software Engineer at Volmatica, February 2025 to present. Previously Associate
Software Engineer at Teknotize, promoted from Full Stack Intern in three
months. BS Computer Science, Bahria University, Islamabad.

## Selected work

### Student Management Platform
React, Node.js, GraphQL, AWS Lambda, SQS, S3, DynamoDB.

Full-stack scheduling for an enterprise tutoring platform serving over 100,000
students per district, with scheduling errors down 90%.

Report exports for large datasets were timing out at API Gateway. Because the
gateway timeout is a platform limit rather than a slow query, the fix was to
move exports out of the request path entirely: a scheduled job builds the
report, writes it to S3, and the client receives a pre-signed URL instead of a
payload. API Gateway is no longer in the data path, so report size stopped
being an availability problem.

Also built validation and consistency checks that block conflicting or
duplicate student assignments, plus an admin dashboard with downloadable
schedule summaries.

### Performance work at Volmatica
Initial page load reduced from 3.5s to 1.8s and Lighthouse from 65 to 92, via
route level React code splitting, lazy loading of below-the-fold components,
and rendering optimization. A separate pass on data fetching moved the app to
TanStack Query with a deliberate cache and invalidation strategy, cutting
redundant API requests by 40% and server load by 20%.

### Shared component library
React, Tailwind, Chakra UI, shadcn/ui, Storybook.

Consolidated duplicated UI primitives into a documented shared library. Feature
development cycles became 30% faster and frontend code duplication dropped 20%.

### ProShop PK
MERN e-commerce application, built while learning that stack.

## How I work

Microservices behind well-defined API contracts. Standardized API response
patterns and reusable middleware. Structured logging and monitoring to cut
incident resolution time. End to end feature ownership from design through
deployment.
